title: The Raiders are already a mess, plus Breanna Stewart reigns with Unrivaled win
content:
The Pulse Newsletter 📣 | This is The Athletic’s daily sports newsletter. Sign up here to receive The Pulse directly in your inbox.

Good morning! Don’t be vague today. Inside:

A busy night begets a check-in before we get really rolling. Quickly:

Time to get messy:

As the NFL offseason churned for a second straight day, another massive name came into focus: Raiders superstar Maxx Crosby, who really appears on his way out of Las Vegas.

Michael Silver wrote a great column with insights into the operation in Vegas, and … it doesn’t seem great. Looking at it through Crosby’s lens is instructive:

Making a significant cameo in this mess: Alex Guerrero, Brady’s right-hand man and “wellness coordinator” who has been the subject of angst within the NFL for a decade now.

Read Michael’s piece here. It’s worth your time. And we’ll probably see Crosby in a new uniform by next week.

A couple of other eyebrow-raising NFL news items from yesterday:

Expect a busy couple of days. Onward

NHL trades finally pop

The NHL trade deadline finally heated up last night with two deals, led by Chicago acquiring forward Andrew Mangiapane and a pick from Edmonton in exchange for fellow forwards Jason Dickinson and Colton Dach. For Chicago, it’s another step in a slow rebuild; for Edmonton, it’s a necessary cost-cutting move for a team that still has Stanley Cup hopes. Both Mangiapane and Dickinson were on our trade board.

Also: Vancouver traded reliable defenseman Tyler Myers to Dallas for two picks. Full details here. The trade deadline is tomorrow at 3 p.m. ET.

Holtz dead at 89
Lou Holtz, iconic college football coach and later beloved commentator, died this week at 89, his family announced yesterday. Holtz’s legacy mainly lies at Notre Dame, where he produced the school’s last national title, Heisman winner and No. 1 recruiting class over an 11-season tenure from 1986 to 1996. I thought Pete Sampson’s obituary for Holtz was great.

📰 Find more news here 24/7.

📺 EPL: Crystal Palace at Tottenham Hotspur
3 p.m. ET on USA Network
I’m so morbidly intrigued by the possible relegation plight for Spurs, and a loss here could absolutely pull a demotion into play. Crikey. Makes for great theater, though.

📺 NHL: Sabres at Penguins
7 p.m. ET on ESPN
Buffalo’s optimism remains one of the NHL’s best stories this year, and the Sabres made a trade yesterday before the deadline to bolster a potential playoff run. Seems like a fun year in Buffalo.

📺 NBA: Lakers at Nuggets
10 p.m. ET on Prime Video
L.A. is 13 games above .500 with two of the most feared athletes on the planet, and yet no one considers the team a real-deal contender. Law Murray wrote this week that the Big 3 — LeBron James, Luka Dončić and Austin Reeves — has been too small this year. I’m curious to watch them against an actual contender.

📺 WBC: Australia vs. Czechia
10 p.m. ET on FS1
The World Baseball Classic continues today, and if you’re a sicko who wants to be up at 5 a.m. watching baseball, it’s actually happening as we send this newsletter (Czechia-Korea). The big slate starts tomorrow.

Get tickets to games like this here.

Dane Brugler debuted his post-combine NFL mock draft yesterday, which is filled with insights from teams, scouts and more. Just click.

Speaking of: So many of the insights we read about NFL prospects come from scouts. It’s almost part of the fabric of our media experience with the league. Jourdan Rodrigue went right to the source for a great feature: on the scouts themselves.

I loved this story on Elsa, the one-named photographer, on how she ended up with the Olympics’ best photo. Read it here.

Nathaniel Salmon (elite name) is 22, from New Zealand and has never played football. How did he end up as a tight end at Washington State?

The plight of the legendary “Dean Dome” at North Carolina is dividing one of college basketball’s most storied fan bases. Brendan Marks has a deeply reported look at the crossroads.

David Aldridge writes about a group of ex-ABA players hoping for a financial long shot from the NBA, decades later. Read that here.

Most-clicked in the newsletter yesterday: Our story on Drew Dalman’s retirement, for which I should issue a mea culpa: The story did not fully explain Dalman’s decision, which we indicated it would, so I did some asking around today. It seems as if everyone is letting Dalman explain at his own pace. We’ll have updates here as we get them.

Most-read on the website yesterday: The mock draft above.

📫 That’s all for now! Say hello at thepulse@theathletic.com, and check out our other newsletters.
